subject: Post-call: NovaMed Diagnostics - evaluation onramp, benchmarks & scoring
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: NovaMed Diagnostics - evaluation onramp, benchmarks & scoring

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off the evaluation on Redwood: 

Recap (what you said):
- Primary goal: automate triage for incoming respiratory diagnostics notes (label = triage recommendation: urgent / routine / follow-up).
- Target latency: < 300ms p95 for single-message lookups, batch scoring acceptable for nightly runs.
- Data constraints: PII must be redacted before upload; NovaMed will provide a sample slice (~2k rows) to validate format.
- Success metrics: precision on Urgent >= 92% on holdout; recall >= 85% for Urgent class; overall macro-F1 >= 0.88.

Redwood recommendation (initial):
- Candidate models to evaluate on Redwood: redwood-13b-quant (lower-cost baseline), redwood-7b-llm-fp16 (fast/cheap), and a higher-capacity open variant we’ll test for headroom (llama-3-13b-raw). We’ll provide model performance/latency tradeoffs in the benchmark report.
- Prompt strategy: classification via structured prompts (system + one-shot examples), plus a compact instruction-only prompt for comparison. We’ll ship two prompt sets: 1) standard instruction + 8-shot examples; 2) minimal instruction for throughput tests.
- Eval plan: run a 3-way model comparison across (a) accuracy/F1 on labeled test set, (b) p95 generation latency under our expected token length distribution, (c) cost per 1k requests.

Attachments I’m including in this thread: novamed-eval-template.csv (format template), redwood-eval-scorer.py (scoring harness stub). Please send a sanitized sample (2k rows) as novamed-sample-cases.csv so we can dry-run ingestion.

Next steps / asks:
1) Emma: share sanitized sample + any existing label schema mapping (ideally CSV with id, text, label, meta).
2) We’ll run an initial sanity pass within 48 hours of receiving the file and share an ingestion report + quick baseline results.
3) Schedule a 30-min kick-off to align on threshold tradeoffs and SLA expectations (I propose Thu or Fri morning PT).

If okay I’ll create a HubSpot playbook and a dedicated Redwood workspace for the project so you can manage runs, secrets, and logs.

Best,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — this looks great and matches our notes. I attached a small sanitized sample (novamed-sample-cases.csv) — 1,950 rows, mixed labels. A couple clarifying Qs before we hand this to our clinical reviewers: 

- Scoring: can you confirm you’ll compute per-class precision/recall and macro-F1? Also want to see confusion matrices for the Urgent class.
- Timeframe: after you do the initial sanity pass, how long to get the 3-model baseline you described? We’re hoping to get initial results within 5 business days.
- Security: our legal asks that Redwood delete temporary inference logs after the run; is that already part of the default workspace settings? We may need a written note for procurement.

Quick note: we have one edge case — notes with multi-encounter text (two separate visits in the same note). Should we include both excerpts as separate rows or annotate with a span? We’ll defer to your best practice.

— Emma
Dr. Emma Lowe
Head of Data Science, NovaMed Diagnostics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-call: NovaMed Diagnostics - evaluation onramp, benchmarks & scoring

Emma — thanks for the sample. I ran a quick schema validation and have the following concrete plan and clarifications for the eval harness and security controls: 

1) Dataset format & ingestion (what we need):
- CSV with columns: id, text, label, encounter_id (optional), redact_flag (yes/no), meta_json (optional). We validated your sample and it needs a small rename of the patient_id column to id (I attached novamed-eval-template.csv).
- For multi-encounter notes: best practice is to split into separate rows per logical encounter (separate id) and include encounter_id so you can map back in post-processing. This makes model scoring and error analysis straightforward.

2) Scoring criteria & metrics:
- Default metrics we’ll compute: per-class precision/recall, macro-F1, class-weighted F1, AUROC for binary urgent vs not-urgent (if you want probability scores), and a confusion matrix export.
- Thresholding: we’ll return both argmax labels and calibrated probabilities. If you want conservative production behavior, we recommend a probability threshold for Urgent tuned to your recall target (we can run a grid search and produce a PR curve).

3) Redwood run config (how we’ll run it):
- Workspace: we’ll provision a dedicated Private workspace (redwood private sandbox) with audit logging off by default for temporary runs. We can set a retention policy to auto-delete logs after X days — I’ll mark 7 days by default and we’ll capture the config in the procurement note.
- Models & resource configs: run three models (redwood-13b-quant, redwood-7b-llm-fp16, llama3-13b-raw) with identical prompt sets. Each run will do: ingestion sanity -> 3-way scoring -> latency/cost profiling using Redwood Optimize heuristics.
- Batching/latency: for your 300ms p95 target we’ll test single-request p95 and a micro-batch throughput test (batch sizes 1, 4, 8) and report impact on p95 and cost.

4) Quality regression checks & monitoring:
- Baseline: first-run models will be our baseline checks. We’ll persist baseline predictions for regression testing.
- Alerting: Redwood Optimize will flag quality drops using a prompt-set based regression test (we’ll ask for ~100 holdout prompts that represent critical clinical edge cases).
- Explainability: we’ll attach nearest-examples and model confidence per prediction to aid clinical review.

5) Timeline:
- Today: validate sample (done) and return notes on schema (this email).
- 48 hrs after we receive sanitized full sample (you indicated ~2k): ingestion + sanity + baseline run setup.
- 5 business days after sample: full 3-model comparison report with scoring, latency, and cost breakdown.

6) Security & procurement note:
- We will set the workspace to delete temporary logs after 7 days. Permanent retention options are configurable and we can include an explicit deletion confirmation for procurement. I’ll generate a short note for legal.

If that timeline looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and tag our SRE for workspace provisioning.

Thanks,
Ben
